note: Motion budgets for this app, from the ios-app-craft kit's defaults (read the kit's note in references/measuring-motion.md). Every number is checked against the median of the runs. 'default' applies to every moment; 'moments' overrides by the names MotionJourneyTests writes; 'journey' limits the mean over moments. Never loosen a budget to pass without a measured reason in moment_notes.

note.move_floor: A frame counts as moving when 0.15% of the screen changes hard, about 100 of the ~70,000 pixels analysed. Under it is noise such as encoder shimmer or a text caret.
note.gap_s: Moving frames less than 60 ms apart (under 4 frames at 60 Hz) are one motion (an episode).
note.pop_area: A pop changes at least 4% of the screen in one frame, about a 120 x 120 pt block on a phone...
note.pop_share: ...and that frame carries 70% or more of its episode's change. An animation spreads its change over many frames, even when the recorder squeezes it into a few; a cut puts it all in one.
note.late_after_s: Change after 250 ms of recorded stillness is content arriving late: a map, chart or image filling in after the page landed. Staggered choreography with shorter pauses is not late.
note.tail_s: An episode that starts within 120 ms of a bigger one is that one's tail, split off by a recorder burst, not a new arrival.
note.analysis_width: Frames are scaled to 180 px wide before comparing. That is enough to see a card move and fast to analyse, and the scaling averages away encoder noise.
note.hard_change: A pixel changed hard when its grey level moved by more than 24 of 255. H.264 noise and soft gradients stay under it.
note.status_bar_share: The top 6% of the frame is left out: the status bar clock and FrameProbe's beacon. It must cover FrameProbe.beaconFrame. On a phone with a Dynamic Island the status bar is about 6.2% of the height. Change it for a device or orientation where it is not.
note.response_window_s: A stall within 400 ms of the finger lift is part of the response. A longer freeze still counts in full.

note.motion_hitch_ms_per_s: Apple's hitch time ratio, counted while pixels move. Apple's lines: under 5 good, 5-10 warning, 10 and up critical (WWDC20 10077, 'Eliminate animation hitches with XCTest'). One missed 60 Hz frame in a one-second moment is already 17, and the simulator drops one now and then at random. So a single moment gets one frame of slack; the journey mean holds the real line.
note.motion_worst_ms: The longest frame while pixels move: at most two missed refreshes in a row at 60 Hz (3 x 16.7 ms).
note.response_stall_ms: The pause between the finger lifting and the screen answering. Under 100 ms feels instant. The simulator, answering XCUITest's accessibility reads, costs about a third more than a phone, hence 120.
note.pops: Nothing snaps or appears from nowhere.
note.late_pct: Nothing arrives after the page lands. 5% of the screen leaves room for a small badge or number settling.
note.settle_ms: First moving pixel to last: long enough for a spring, short enough not to drag. Equal to MotionTestCase.settle (1.4 s); flings get MotionTestCase.flingSettle (3.0 s) and 3000. A budget longer than its moment's window can never fail, so keep them equal. A moment still moving when its window closes is flagged in the report's warnings.

moments.note: Overrides by moment name. null, or 1000 and up on a metric that is not in ms, means 'not meaningful here': not budgeted, not checked against the baseline, and left out of the journey mean. A duration of 1000 ms or more is a real budget. "in_journey": false leaves the whole moment out of the journey mean; use it only for one-off costs like the launch. Loosen a moment only with a measured reason in moment_notes. Example: the session's first open of a page drawn unseen before its flight was allowed 140 ms, since a second open measured under 100.

regression.note: A metric fails when new > old * (1 + ratio) + abs. abs 17 is one 60 Hz frame and 25 about one and a half. pops 0/0: any new pop fails. Ratios near 0.5 absorb the simulator's run-to-run noise on small numbers. Tune them from repeated runs of an unchanged build: the tolerance must sit above that noise and below one real regression. A metric with no entry here gets ratio 0.25, abs 1.

note.motion_hitch_ms_per_s: The mean over moments, launch left out. 7 is the reference app's line, set when the launch was still counted: 5.29 with it, 1.89 without, since its 97 ms/s launch was 64% of the mean. With the launch out, 7 is loose. Once your baseline is in, tighten toward Apple's 'good' line of 5.
note.response_stall_ms: The mean response, launch left out. Most taps answer within a few frames: the reference app measured 52 with the launch and 43 without.
note.late_pct: The mean late area, leaving out moments where late_pct is not meaningful.

moment_notes.launch: Process start and the first build of every screen. The loose budgets catch disasters, and the baseline catches drift. Left out of the journey mean.
moment_notes.harness_idle_tap: A tap on inert text: nothing moves. Its response_stall_ms is XCUITest's own cost, the floor under every other response number.
moment_notes.home_scroll: A fling. Its deceleration after a pause is not late content, so late_pct is not meaningful, and settling takes 2.5-3 s.
moment_notes.card_open: The session's first open of a card: the page is built and measured on the tap's frame (response), then the pieces fly for 480 ms and the page-only content arrives by 735 ms. Pops must be 0: t = 0 is the card, landing is the page.
moment_notes.card_back: Back by the page's button: the card is measured again, the pieces fly home, the bar returns half way.
moment_notes.card_open_again: A warm open: one-time costs are paid, so this is the open's steady state.
moment_notes.card_swipe_back: Back by the left-edge swipe: the page shrinks with the finger, then its pieces fly home from the shrunk positions. XCUITest's gesture synthesis makes this the noisiest moment run to run.
moment_notes.tab_settings: A kept tab sliding in (built after launch, unseen).
moment_notes.tab_home: Back to a kept tab: nothing is rebuilt.
